locator: pp.52–55 p.53 (definition) and p.54 ('David Armstrong was a naturalist by the definition used in this paper (2010, p.1)')
interpretation: Murphy defines naturalism, for his paper, as the doctrine that nothing exists apart from spatio-temporal objects and that all spatio-temporal objects are contingent, and reports that Armstrong was a naturalist in this sense, citing Sketch for a Systematic Metaphysics (2010), p. 1. Read as N1 with P = spatio-temporal, dropping the contingency conjunct (weaker than the definition). It is Armstrong's view as Murphy reports it, not Armstrong's wording: Armstrong 1997 and 2010 are not pinned. Murphy does not say which sense of spatio-temporal is meant, so P is left to DISAMB-SPATIOTEMPORAL. Murphy adopts the definition for the paper's purposes only and does not assert naturalism himself.
attribution: The passage states that Armstrong held that nothing exists apart from spatio-temporal objects, which is the premise with P = spatio-temporal.
